claims: The Artemis II mission broke the human spaceflight distance record set by Apollo 13 in 1970 on April 6, 2026.
Apollo 13 reached 248,655 statute miles from Earth in 1970.
The Artemis II crew surpassed 248,655 miles from Earth.
The Artemis II crew reached a maximum distance of approximately 252,756 miles from Earth.
Artemis II reached roughly 252,756 miles (approximately 406,771+ km) on April 6, 2026.
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew achieved the distance record during a flyby of the far side of the Moon.
The Artemis II crew experienced a 40-minute communications blackout while passing behind the moon.
During the communications blackout, the Artemis II crew observed the far side of the moon.
During the communications blackout, the Artemis II crew observed a total solar eclipse.
The Artemis II crew expressed hope that this new record will be broken again soon by future generations
